title: Avaloq consumes Flowable inside its own core banking product, so it is a vendor and not a delivery channel
content:
Avaloq appears in the Flowable Partner Finder, but the entry describes an OEM relationship: the engine is embedded in Avaloq's own core banking software. The research draws the conclusion directly — vendor, not an integrator — and records 2,000+ staff.

The distinction decides what kind of conversation is possible. In this corpus an integrator is a firm that could place a Powerhouse component inside a client project it is already delivering; an OEM would instead have to adopt that component into its own product roadmap, on its own release cycle, against its own build-versus-buy logic. Directory membership looks identical in both cases, which is exactly why the flag records the difference explicitly.

It is also worth noting how thin the underlying provenance is. The row was mined from the vendor's partner page on 2026-08-18 and was not imprint-swept, so no principal or contact address was resolved. Two further OEM entries in the same sweep — Exentra and eligamo — carry the same shape, which means the Partner Finder cannot be read as a channel list without first separating the product vendors from the delivery firms.
